name: Joe Moss
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Extend (San Francisco)
profile: Joe Moss co-founded Extend, a San Francisco company that sells product-protection plans (extended warranties) and shipping protection through online merchants. CEO Woody Levin leads the company. Extend began selling in 2019 and raised a $260M Series C at a valuation of over $1.6B in May 2021. Moss leads product.
interesting_fact: Extend became a unicorn in about 27 months of operation. CEO Woody Levin pitched it as the 'Apple Care' for everything that isn't an Apple product.
notes: Low public profile. Moss's prior roles (reportedly DocuSign product and an earlier startup) appear only on aggregator sites and could not be verified, so they are left out. No published press email was found on extend.com. The best route is the company contact form, or via CEO Woody Levin.

name: Rick Song
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Persona (identity verification platform, San Francisco)
profile: Rick Song spent about five years at Square as an engineer and early Square Capital team member. In 2018 he co-founded Persona with CTO Charles Yeh to build configurable identity-verification building blocks. In April 2025 Persona raised a $200M Series D led by Founders Fund and Ribbit at a $2B valuation, pitching a 'verified identity layer' for an AI-agent internet.
interesting_fact: Persona's $200M Series D (April 2025) valued it at $2B, up from $1.5B in its 2021 Series C. The pitch is building the verified identity layer for an increasingly AI-driven internet.
deep_cut_fact: At Square he worked on lending fraud at Square Capital and on trust and safety for the Caviar food-delivery business, which exposed him to many identity-verification use cases. He calls himself 'slightly obsessed' with pre-mortems and jokes that Persona is 'an entire company of people who have never done startups'.
notes: The press email came from the withpersona.com/about page text as returned by search; a direct fetch of the page was blocked (403). He has done podcasts (First Round 'In Depth' ep. 22, Product Market Fit Show), so he is receptive to founder-story interviews.

name: Oliver Kent-Braham
current_role: Co-founder and CEO (also described as co-CEO), Marshmallow (UK car and home insurer for newcomers)
profile: Oliver Kent-Braham is a south-west Londoner and briefly a banker at Investec. In 2017 he co-founded Marshmallow with his twin Alexander and engineer David Goate to make car insurance fairer for people who have moved to the UK. Marshmallow became a licensed insurer in 2021. Its April 2025 $90M raise valued it at about $2B, with roughly 1M customers and a ~$500M revenue run rate.
interesting_fact: Marshmallow insures roughly one million people, up from about 100,000 in 2021, and says it is profitable on a ~$500M annual revenue run rate. Kent-Braham calls migration 'a huge opportunity'.
deep_cut_fact: In the early days the founders worked from the lobby of a Virgin Active gym. Kent-Braham paid for an £80 membership, which got the team a desk plus sauna and steam room access: 'the cheapest office space'. The idea came from a Canadian friend who kept getting sky-high car insurance quotes.
notes: His twin Alexander is the other co-founder (internal/product side); Oliver handles external matters and fundraising. No press email was found on marshmallow.com. Sources vary on the founding year (2016 or 2017).

name: Peter Godman
current_role: Unknown; former co-founder, founding CEO and later CTO of Qumulo (left November 2018)
profile: Peter Godman is a Seattle systems engineer. At Isilon he led several major releases of the OneFS distributed file system, then was VP engineering and CEO at Corensic. In 2012 he co-founded Qumulo, a scale-out file-storage company, with fellow Isilon alumni Neil Fachan and Aaron Passey. He served as CEO until Bill Richter took over in 2016, then as CTO until he left in late 2018.
interesting_fact: He is credited with inventing 18 patented technologies. At Corensic he brought what was billed as the world's first thin-hypervisor-based product to market.
deep_cut_fact: When he left Qumulo after nearly seven years, CEO Bill Richter called him 'a visionary, an inspiration and a good friend' and wished him 'a well deserved break, time with his family and his next adventure.'
notes: No public reporting on his activities since leaving Qumulo in 2018 was found, so alive is marked unknown (no death reports found either). Very low public profile; no verified personal site or social accounts found. Relevant to the data-center angle as a storage and file-system veteran.
